    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). This month is missing *Nat Mach Intell*. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: JAMA 136, Nature 102, Nucleic Acids Res 100, Science 90, Bioinformatics 80, Blood 78.

## 3. The evidence that moved it











**Two benchmark metrics were declared invalid in the same journal in the same
month.** [40739072](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40739072/) (*Nat Biotechnol*) finds that the
silhouette-based metrics underpinning single-cell integration benchmarks are
invalid, undermining published method rankings;
[40854979](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40854979/) finds that perturbation-prediction benchmarks are
inflated by systematic non-perturbation variation, so reported gains over
trivial baselines are not real. Together with April's
[40500472](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40500472/), three cards in three months say the same thing about
different subfields: the leaderboard, not the method, is what has been broken.

**Mouse models were told they are not the human tumour.**
[42156893](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42156893/) (*Nat Immunol*) states that mouse tumour models do not
assemble the same immune microenvironment as human tumours. This is the single
card that bears on the largest volume of work in this corpus. The templated
preclinical block — nominate a target, reverse suppression, synergise with
anti-PD-1 in mice — runs at roughly twenty papers a month across the oncology
journals, and this paper says its readout system does not reproduce the thing
it is modelling. It does not make that literature wrong; it makes the step from
that literature to a trial the unvalidated one, which is exactly where
`next-gen-checkpoints` keeps failing.

**A widely repeated survival claim was attributed to selection bias.**
[42330421](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42330421/) (*Cancer Discov*) reports that the survival benefit of
incidental COVID mRNA vaccination around checkpoint therapy is selection bias,
not immune synergy. The original observation entered this corpus as a support in
October 2025 ([41125896](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41125896/), mRNA vaccines sensitizing tumours to
checkpoint blockade). Eight months from striking result to attributed artifact is
the fastest full cycle the corpus has recorded, and it is the reason the
`stance` field exists. What it is not is a card against neoantigen vaccines. The
exposure is non-tumour-specific mRNA vaccination given alongside checkpoint
therapy, and it bears on neither the size nor the predictability of the
neoantigen target space, which is what `neoantigen-vaccines` claims. It was
counting as a refutation of a thread it does not address, and it is now neutral
there.

**Cell therapy reached ten years.** [42341302](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42341302/) (*NEJM*) follows 38
patients a median of 10.1 years after a single tisagenlecleucel infusion. No
relapse occurred beyond 5.4 years, and ten-year lymphoma-free survival was 32%
in large B-cell lymphoma and 47% in follicular lymphoma. The late-toxicity
column is on the same page: a second primary cancer in 9 patients (21%
cumulative incidence at ten years), 18% non-relapse mortality, and persistent
B-cell aplasia in 44% of long-term responders. Every durability and
late-toxicity argument in this thread now has a number to attach to, and the two
sets of numbers have to be quoted together.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This subsection opened by reporting that PRESERVE-003
    ([41896648](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41896648/)) showed a
    next-generation pH-sensitive anti-CTLA-4 failing to outperform chemotherapy
    after PD-1 failure, and read it as "the third time in the corpus that a
    checkpoint target survives a failure by being reformatted and then fails
    again in the new format". The trial reports the opposite. Its title is
    "Gotistobart or docetaxel" — trial, comparator, population, stage, and no
    result — and a failure was supplied for it. Stage 1 reports an
    overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.46. The reformat-and-fail argument has no
    instance here and is withdrawn; the card is now `supports`, and the month's
    next-generation checkpoint cards no longer sit in this subsection.

What the month actually landed on `next-gen-checkpoints` is three positive
readouts, kept here with their sign corrected rather than moved.
[41896648](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41896648/) (*Nat Med*) reports stage 1 of PRESERVE-003:
gotistobart, a pH-sensitive anti-CTLA-4 that selectively depletes regulatory T
cells inside the tumour, against docetaxel in metastatic squamous NSCLC that had
progressed on both PD-(L)1 blockade and platinum chemotherapy. At 14.5 months'
median follow-up, median overall survival was not reached with gotistobart
against 10.0 months with docetaxel (hazard ratio 0.46, 95% CI 0.25-0.84, nominal
two-sided P = 0.0102), with grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events in
42% against 49%. Read it for what it is: 87 patients, stage 1 of two, a nominal
P value and a dose-confirmation objective. But it is the engineering fix — pH
sensitivity, meant to widen CTLA-4's therapeutic window — producing a result in
the population where the existing generation has already failed, which is the
scenario this thread was built to watch for.

Alongside it, [42284198](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42284198/) (*Blood*) brings PD-1/TIGIT-knockdown CD19
CAR-T to the clinic, merging the checkpoint and cell-therapy threads: if the
receptor cannot be blocked systemically, delete it in the cell you are already
engineering. And [42218899](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42218899/) (*Lancet*) reports the interim
overall-survival analysis of HARMONi-6, in which the PD-1xVEGF bispecific
ivonescimab plus chemotherapy beat the PD-1 antibody tislelizumab plus
chemotherapy in advanced squamous NSCLC — 27.9 against 23.7 months, hazard ratio
0.66 (95% CI 0.50-0.87), at the cost of more grade 3 or higher treatment-related
adverse events and more haemorrhage. That is the head-to-head comparator design
against an active checkpoint antibody that the earlier anti-TIGIT programmes
never got, and it is the design that makes a next-generation claim checkable.

### (b) Method credibility

[42086853](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42086853/) (*Nat Genet*): age structure distinguishes selection
from causation, and recurrence-based driver calling systematically misassigns
drivers. Recurrence is how essentially every cancer driver list in use was
built.

[42062553](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42062553/) (*Nat Methods*): imaging spatial transcriptomics carries
substantial per-gene false positives and transcript misassignment between
neighbouring cells. This is the fourth spatial-transcriptomics credibility card
in six months, after January's differential-expression false discovery rate,
February's segmentation-error dominance and April's version-dependence. Spatial
transcriptomics is simultaneously the most productive method area in this corpus
and the one with the most evidence against its own base operations.
